Active balancing
balancing that moves charge from high cell groups to low ones through switched capacitors, inductors or small transformers, at up to a few amperes with 80–90 % efficiency.
Arc flash
the burst of heat, light and molten metal released when a short circuit is drawn across battery terminals or busbars; a 72 V pack can deliver several thousand amperes.
AVD extinguisher
an aqueous vermiculite dispersion extinguisher, used to cool and coat small lithium-ion packs.
Back-EMF constant (Ke)
the back-EMF a motor generates per unit of angular speed, in V·s/rad; in SI units numerically equal to the torque constant for an ideal machine.
Battery-to-wheel efficiency
the fraction of energy taken from the traction battery that reaches the rear tyre, typically about 80 %.
Black mass
the shredded mixture of electrode materials from recycled cells, leached to recover lithium, nickel, cobalt and manganese.
Calendar ageing
capacity loss and resistance growth that proceed with time even when a battery is not used, faster at high temperature and high state of charge.
Cell-to-pack mass ratio
the fraction of a battery pack's mass that is cells; typically 60–75 % for two-wheeler packs.
Clarke and Park transforms
the coordinate changes used in field-oriented control: three phase currents to two stationary components, then to the rotor-fixed d and q components.
Coercivity
a magnet's resistance to demagnetisation by an opposing field; in NdFeB it falls by about 0.5–0.6 % per kelvin.
Common-port BMS
a BMS that charges and discharges through the same terminals and switches; a separate-port BMS has its own, usually lower-rated, charge path.
Current interrupt device (CID)
a pressure-operated disconnect inside a cylindrical cell that opens the circuit before the cell vents.
Curie temperature
the temperature above which a permanent magnet loses its magnetism entirely; 310–400 °C for NdFeB, although damage occurs far below it.
Cycle ageing
capacity loss caused by charging and discharging, depending on depth of discharge, current and temperature.
Duty cycle
the fraction of each PWM switching period during which the high-side switch conducts; it sets the average phase voltage.
Efficiency map
a plot of contours of constant motor efficiency on the torque-speed plane.
Four-wire measurement
a resistance measurement that injects current through one pair of leads and measures voltage with another, so lead resistance does not affect milliohm readings.
Lorentz force
the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field, F = B × I × L, the origin of motor torque.
Maximum continuous rated power
the power an electric drive can sustain for 30 minutes on a test bench (UNECE R85), used for vehicle category limits.
Open-circuit voltage (OCV)
the voltage of a cell at rest with no current; used with a lookup table to estimate state of charge.
Passive balancing
balancing that bleeds charge from high cell groups as heat through resistors, typically at 30–200 mA near the top of charge.
Performance ratio
the fraction of a solar array's rated output actually delivered after temperature, soiling, inverter and wiring losses, typically 0.7–0.8.
Pole pair
one north and one south magnetic pole on a motor rotor; the electrical frequency equals pole pairs times revolutions per second.
Reluctance torque
torque produced by rotor iron tending to align with the stator field; present in interior permanent-magnet motors where Lq exceeds Ld.
Remanence
the flux density a magnet retains with no applied field; 1.2–1.45 T for NdFeB, falling about 0.11–0.12 % per kelvin.
Second life
reuse of a retired traction battery, typically at 70–80 % SOH, in less demanding stationary storage.
Shoot-through
simultaneous conduction of the high-side and low-side switches of one inverter leg, which short-circuits the DC link.
Slip
the amount by which the rotor of an induction motor runs slower than the rotating field, typically 2–5 % at rated load.
Space-vector PWM
a modulation method for three-phase inverters that uses the DC-link voltage about 15 % more effectively than simple sinusoidal PWM.
Surface permanent-magnet (SPM) motor
a motor with magnets bonded to the rotor surface; magnetically round, so torque comes only from the magnets.
Tank-to-wheel efficiency
the fraction of fuel energy that reaches the rear tyre of a petrol motorcycle, about 10–20 % in urban riding.
Live-dead-live
the zero-voltage verification method of proving a meter on a known live source, testing the isolated circuit, then proving the meter again.
Axial-flux motor
a motor in which flux crosses a flat disc-shaped air gap parallel to the shaft, giving high torque in a short axial length.
Induction motor
a magnet-free motor in which the stator field induces currents in a squirrel-cage rotor that runs with slip.
